# Implemented services and features

TinyStack implements **121 service APIs** with **2,950 selected operations**.

This catalogue records the capabilities available in the current checkout. Each service implements a subset;
its reference documents supported operations, inputs, and behavior limits. Execution modes show when a
feature manages records or needs a Docker runtime.

## Shared platform features

| Feature | Implemented behavior | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTPS and local CA | Optional HTTPS gateway with a persisted ECDSA P-256 local CA, a leaf per requested AWS, LocalStack or localhost name, extra DNS/IP names, supplied certificate/key support, and CA PEM export. Trust, DNS and port forwarding remain manual. | [Details](../guides/tls.md) |
| Fault injection | Ordered gateway rules inject protocol-correct AWS errors and cancellable latency by service, operation, Region and account, with probability, startup configuration, reset restoration, diagnostics and LocalStack Chaos API aliases. | [Details](../guides/fault-injection.md) |
| AWS wire protocols | AWS JSON 1.0/1.1, AWS Query, EC2 Query, REST XML/JSON, and Smithy RPC v2 CBOR through generated bindings. | [Details](../architecture/request-flow.md) |
| Identity and resource scope | Configured access-key accounts, 12-digit access keys that are their own account ID, IAM/STS credential lookup, regional and account-wide scopes, optional SigV4 verification, and identity-policy evaluation with off, soft and enforce modes. | [Details](../architecture/identity.md) |
| Transactional storage and persistence | Atomic callback transactions, in-memory storage, and optional SQLite commit persistence with resource reload on restart; runtime and in-flight state have separate limits. | [Details](../guides/persistence.md) |
| Cloudscape console | AWS-style dark dashboard with configurable widgets, a favorites bar of starred services, visit history, categorized service catalog with AWS icons, shared top-bar account/Region menus with configured-account choices, resource inventory/details, IAM, S3, SQS, SNS, Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CloudWatch Logs and CloudWatch metrics/alarms/dashboard, API Gateway HTTP/REST, Step Functions, EC2/VPC management workflows, and account-wide Budgets with actual spend, Cost Explorer charts and fixture management, and CUR report management, in-memory signed root console sessions for verify mode, IAM authorization status and explained request decisions, recent requests, delivery history, and metrics through a separately served web console. | [Details](../guides/diagnostics.md) |
| Diagnostics | Health/resource endpoints, bounded request and delivery logs, outbound message inspection (email, SMS, Cognito codes) with LocalStack-compatible SES and SNS aliases, model-sensitive body redaction, and Prometheus request metrics. | [Details](../guides/diagnostics.md) |
| Init hooks and reset | LocalStack-style boot, start, ready and shutdown scripts (also read from /etc/localstack/init) with a status endpoint, idempotent IAM/S3/SQS sample data in the development example config, and a POST reset endpoint that clears all stored state and can re-run the ready scripts. | [Details](../guides/init-hooks.md) |
| CLI and SDK clients | Local endpoint overrides for AWS clients, CLI wrappers (aws, terraform, sam, cdk), and generated Go SDK-compatible APIs. | [Details](../getting-started/clients.md) |
| Infrastructure workflows | Selected Terraform AWS provider workflows, AWS SAM and CDK (bootstrap and deploy) through the registered CloudFormation resource-type subset. | [Details](../guides/infrastructure.md) |
| Runtime adapters | Docker Lambda execution and opt-in ECS Docker tasks, EKS k3s clusters, and ElastiCache Docker nodes; default optional adapters manage records. | [Details](../guides/runtimes.md) |
| Cross-service event delivery | Supported notification, rule, and event-source workflows connect local service implementations and record delivery outcomes. | [Details](../guides/events.md) |
| Console single sign-on | Optional OpenID Connect sign-in to the console (authorization code with PKCE, any compliant provider such as Authelia, Zitadel, Keycloak, Authentik, Okta or Entra ID). Provider groups grant all matching IAM roles, deduplicated in configuration order; people with several roles choose an account and role in an access portal and can switch within their server-owned allowed set from the Account menu. Only the active role grants administrative access. The person gets the selected role's temporary STS credentials, so IAM authorization and the request inspector apply per person, and the administrative endpoints require an administrator's session or root credentials. `tinystack login` signs the AWS CLI in the same way through the device authorization flow, with HTTPS outside loopback, single-use fresh tokens and private atomic credential caches and an explicit --role selection for multi-role users. Enforced member inventory omits details and evaluates request conditions; mapped role deletion invalidates old federated credentials. | [Details](../guides/sso.md) |
| Console CloudShell | A browser terminal in console builds that executes the real host AWS CLI with streamed output, quotes and escapes, a scrubbed environment and a forced TinyStack API endpoint. Local mode uses the selected account; verify mode issues short-lived STS credentials for the verified console principal so normal gateway IAM applies. Every CLI command runs with aws_completer completion unless console.cloudshell.allow lists service:command patterns such as s3:*, which then limit both commands and completion; with OIDC/SSO CloudShell is administrator-only. Command bodies and output are redacted in the inspector, requests are capped at 64 KiB, and at most four commands run concurrently. AWS CLI v2 must be installed separately; the Docker image does not include it. No shell features or interactive prompts; history stays in memory. The opening banner identifies the console principal and account. Silent successful commands print a dim (no output) line. | [Details](../guides/cloudshell.md) |
| Optional DNS listener | Opt-in UDP/TCP split DNS for AWS endpoint and resource names, default-account Route 53 records, and upstream forwarding. HTTP gateway; default HTTPS clients need a trusted TLS reverse proxy and port mapping. | [Details](../guides/dns.md) |
| Instance and container metadata | EC2 IMDSv1/v2 under /_tinystack/imds and an optional dedicated /latest listener, with explicit instance selection and STS instance-profile credentials. Verify mode requires the dedicated listener for IMDS credentials. Docker ECS tasks receive host-reachable metadata v4 and task-role credential endpoints; tokens are removed when tasks stop. | [Details](../guides/metadata.md) |

## Service features

Use the [support matrix](index.md) to compare operation counts and execution modes.

### Analytics

#### AWS Lake Formation

Store data lake settings, S3 registrations, permission grants and LF-tags without enforcing access or running queries.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 19.

- Nineteen REST JSON operations with AWS SDK v2 lifecycle coverage and Terraform settings, resource, permissions, LF-tag and resource LF-tag resources.
- Get/PutDataLakeSettings; new accounts default to IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS with ALL for new databases and tables; settings replace the complete record.
- Register/Deregister/List/DescribeResource for S3 ARNs with explicit or service-linked IAM role and recorded hybrid access flag.
- Grant/Revoke/ListPermissions and BatchGrant/BatchRevokePermissions with principal validation, exactly one resource selector, permission validation and per-entry batch failures.
- Catalog, database, table, table wildcard, named columns/column wildcard, registered data location and LF-tag grant selectors; database/table references must exist in TinyStack Glue.
- Create/Get/Update/Delete/ListLFTags and Add/Remove/GetResourceLFTags for databases, named tables and named columns; one value per assigned key, database-to-table inheritance and assigned-only reads.
- LF-tag value deletion removes stale assignments and matching LF-tag grants; deterministic token pagination and account/Region isolation.
- Inventory reports RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false; LF-tags are classification metadata rather than native AWS resource tags.

[Supported operations](lakeformation.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](lakeformation.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Amazon EMR

Records only, no Hadoop/Spark runtime: store classic EMR clusters, synthetic capacity and simulated steps.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 33.

- Thirty-three JSON 1.1 ElasticMapReduce operations with elasticmapreduce signing: cluster creation, describe/list, termination protection, visibility, concurrency and termination.
- Instance group auto-scaling policies (put, remove, list) and cluster managed scaling policies (put, get, remove); records only, scaling never executes.
- Account and Region block public access configuration (get, put) with default permitted rule ranges; records only, security group rules are not enforced.
- Read-driven STARTING → BOOTSTRAPPING → RUNNING → WAITING and TERMINATING → TERMINATED transitions with reasons and timestamps; clusters without keep-alive terminate after all steps finish.
- Fixed EMR 6.x and 7.x release labels, application/configuration metadata, EC2 subnet and security group existence/VPC validation, IAM service role and instance profile role validation, S3 log bucket validation and security configuration references; release list includes EMR 7.14.0.
- Instance group and fleet add/list/resize, synthetic instance IDs and subnet private addresses, bootstrap action metadata; no compute is allocated.
- Step submission, describe/list filters and cancellation; simulated PENDING → RUNNING → COMPLETED without executing scripts; ActionOnFailure concurrency validation and failure policy handling.
- Security configuration create/describe/list/delete with JSON validation, cluster tags with shared limits, inventory, Resource Groups integration, console and Terraform cluster/security configuration/instance group coverage.
- Cluster state and creation time filters, step ID/state filters and Marker pagination with 50 records per page; account and Region isolation; idle auto-termination evaluated on reads.

[Supported operations](emr.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](emr.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Amazon EMR Serverless

Store Spark and Hive application and job-run metadata without executing code or provisioning compute.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 14.

- Fourteen pinned REST JSON operations: application create/get/update/delete/list/start/stop, job start/get/list/cancel and three native tag operations.
- Application transitions complete synchronously: creation returns CREATED, start returns STARTED and stop returns STOPPED; deletion completes TERMINATED and removes the application and its job history.
- Application release label, type, architecture, worker and maximum capacity, auto-start/stop and network configuration validation and metadata; updates require CREATED or STOPPED.
- Jobs report SUBMITTED, PENDING, SCHEDULED, RUNNING and SUCCESS on successive GetJobRun calls; cancellation synchronously returns CANCELLED and terminal jobs cannot be cancelled.
- Spark submit and Hive driver metadata, application configuration overrides, execution role ARN validation, job timeout metadata and explicit simulated state details.
- Idempotent create/update/job-start client tokens, conflict detection for changed parameters, pagination (default and maximum 50), application/job state filters.
- Application and job ARN tags with the shared 50-tag limit, Resource Groups Tagging API integration, scoped inventory with RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false, console listing and Terraform aws_emrserverless_application.

[Supported operations](emrserverless.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](emrserverless.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink

Store Managed Flink applications, configuration, versions and snapshots without running jobs.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 20.

- Twenty AWS JSON 1.1 operations: application create/describe/list/update/delete/start/stop, describe/list versions, add/delete VPC and CloudWatch logging configuration, create/describe/list/delete snapshots and three native tag operations.
- FLINK-1_6, FLINK-1_8, FLINK-1_11, FLINK-1_13, FLINK-1_15, FLINK-1_18, FLINK-1_19 and FLINK-1_20 runtimes from the pinned model; STREAMING mode only.
- Deterministic READY to STARTING to RUNNING and RUNNING to STOPPING to READY lifecycle; updates enter UPDATING, preserve the final running state, increment the version and retain historical configuration; Force stop accepts READY.

- User snapshots require RUNNING and contain READY metadata with the application version; tag limits, inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API and console integration.
- IAM role ARN validation and gateway PassRole checks for CreateApplication and UpdateApplication; Terraform application and snapshot coverage.

#### Athena

Query local S3 data through the Glue catalog using an in-memory SQLite SQL engine.

**Execution:** SQLite SQL engine with local S3 reads/writes and Glue catalog updates. **Selected operations:** 25.

- Workgroups, named queries, query execution metadata, pagination and client tokens.
- SELECT queries over CSV, delimited text, JSON and Parquet, including gzip text and SNAPPY/GZIP/ZSTD Parquet pages.
- Glue catalog DDL, SHOW, DESCRIBE, MSCK REPAIR and partition changes.
- CTAS to Parquet, JSON or TEXTFILE, WITH NO DATA, and INSERT INTO SELECT or VALUES.
- Partitioned writes create Hive prefixes and Glue partitions; row update counts are retained.
- Query results are retained and written to the configured S3 output location.

[Supported operations](athena.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](athena.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Data Firehose

Buffer direct or Kinesis records and deliver them to S3.

**Execution:** Local behavior. **Selected operations:** 12.

- Delivery streams, tags, direct puts and batch puts.
- Background buffering and S3 output after size/time thresholds.
- Kinesis source polling and Lambda processing through the shared caller.
- With authorization on, S3 writes and Lambda processor calls assume the destination's role, whose trust policy must allow firehose.amazonaws.com for the delivery stream, and are decided by the role's policies; a denied processor call fails its records with Lambda.InvokeAccessDenied and a denied write is recorded as a failed delivery.
- PutRecord and PutRecordBatch resolve delivery stream ARNs and tags for resource-scoped identity and delivery-role policies.

[Supported operations](firehose.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](firehose.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Glue

Manage the Data Catalog, classify and crawl S3 data, and orchestrate local Python shell ETL jobs and workflows.

**Execution:** Records / local S3 crawling / optional local Python host execution. **Selected operations:** 70.

- Database CRUD, tags and pagination.
- Table CRUD and batch deletion.
- Partition CRUD, batch operations and partition listings.
- Names are normalized to lowercase; deleting a database removes its tables and partitions.
- Job CRUD, batch reads, tag-filtered listings and whole-definition updates with IAM role validation; GlueVersion is retained if omitted from JobUpdate, as AWS documents.
- Python shell jobs fetch scripts from TinyStack S3 and run with the selected Lambda local host executor.
- Durable run states, merged arguments, non-overridable arguments, minute timeouts, process-group stop, retries and concurrency limits.
- Complete stdout and stderr are published after each attempt to /aws-glue/python-jobs/output and /aws-glue/python-jobs/error, using JobRunId streams.
- ON_DEMAND, five-minute-or-slower UTC cron and job-state CONDITIONAL triggers, using the shared schedule parser.
- Workflows with on-demand and scheduled source triggers, conditional chains, run properties, graphs, statistics, stopping and concurrency limits.
- Jobs, triggers and workflows support tags, resource inventory and CloudFormation.
- CSV and JSON custom classifier CRUD, versions, timestamps and pagination; custom classifiers run before built-ins in crawler order.
- S3 crawler CRUD, batches, tag-filtered listings, schedules, stop, history and metrics; IAM roles, S3 buckets and custom classifiers must exist.
- Shared tabular inference for CSV, TSV, pipe and semicolon text, JSON objects/lines with nested Hive types, Parquet and gzip text; Hive and unnamed folder partitions.
- Crawlers publish tables and partitions to the same catalog Athena reads, with SerDes, classification and file statistics.
- Schema update and table deletion/deprecation policies and incremental new-folder crawls; crawler conditions and actions participate in workflow graphs and statistics.
- Crawler tags, inventory, Resource Groups Tagging, AWS::Glue::Crawler and CSV/JSON AWS::Glue::Classifier CloudFormation resources.

[Supported operations](glue.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](glue.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### EventBridge

Route events through local buses, patterns, rules, schedules, archives, and replays.

**Execution:** Local behavior. **Selected operations:** 41.

- Default and custom buses, rules, targets and input transformers.
- Pattern matching shared with other event services.
- SQS, SNS and Lambda targets in the same account and region.
- Connections (API key, Basic and OAuth client credentials, with invocation header, query string and body parameters) and API destinations; Describe never returns secrets, and DeauthorizeConnection removes the credentials as AWS does.
- API destination targets make a real HTTP request with the rendered event as the body: the target's HttpParameters fill the endpoint's * wildcards and add headers and query string parameters, the connection adds its parameters (which win) and its authorization, OAuth access tokens are cached until they expire, and a response other than 2xx fails the delivery into the retry and dead-letter path (5xx, 401, 407, 409 and 429 are retried, other statuses go to the dead-letter queue at once).
- Scheduled rules, durable retry records and SQS dead-letter queues.
- Archives and synchronous replay.
- AWS-style console for scoped event buses, rule patterns and schedules, nondelivering pattern tests, Lambda/SQS/SNS target selection and input/retry options, tags, explicit test-event publication and rule/bus delivery inspection.
- Gateway bus and rule resource-policy enforcement, explicit Deny precedence, and same-region cross-account bus ARN publication and rule management.
- With authorization on, SQS, SNS and Lambda targets without a role, and dead-letter queues, need their resource policy to allow events.amazonaws.com with the rule as aws:SourceArn; enforce mode fails the invocation into the existing retry and dead-letter path with the ERROR_CODE NO_PERMISSIONS, soft mode records the denied check.
- Targets with a RoleArn assume that role, whose trust policy must allow events.amazonaws.com for the rule (aws:SourceArn) and account, and are then decided by the role's policies and the target's resource policy; a role that cannot be assumed reports FAILED_TO_ASSUME_ROLE.

[Supported operations](eventbridge.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](eventbridge.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### EventBridge Pipes

Connect SQS queues and Kinesis or DynamoDB streams to targets with filtering and Lambda enrichment.

**Execution:** Local behavior. **Selected operations:** 10.

- CreatePipe, DescribePipe, UpdatePipe, DeletePipe, ListPipes with filters and pagination, StartPipe and StopPipe.
- Pipes settle at once in RUNNING or STOPPED; responses report the transitional state.
- Tags on pipes through TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource, and through the Resource Groups Tagging API.
- SQS sources read in-process; messages are deleted after delivery or when a filter drops them.
- Kinesis and DynamoDB stream sources with TRIM_HORIZON or LATEST and a per-pipe cursor.
- FilterCriteria event patterns shared with Lambda event source mappings.
- Lambda enrichment, and InputTemplate with JSON paths and aws.pipes variables on enrichment and target.
- Lambda, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Step Functions and Kinesis targets, called in-process; Lambda and Step Functions receive the batch as a JSON array.
- Resources appear in the resource inventory.
- With authorization on, enrichment and target calls assume the pipe's role, whose trust policy must allow pipes.amazonaws.com for the pipe (aws:SourceArn) and account, and are decided by the role's policies; a denied delivery is a failed delivery that the next visit retries, and soft mode records the check.
- With authorization on, source reads (SQS ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage and GetQueueAttributes; stream describe, iterator and record reads) are made as the pipe's role too, checked once every 30 seconds per pipe, role and source, including denials; role or source changes force a recheck, deletion drops its entry and reset clears every entry; a denied pipe moves nothing.

### Compute

#### AWS App Runner

Store App Runner services, revisioned configurations, connections and VPC connectors as metadata over AWS JSON 1.0.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 28.

- Twenty-eight pinned-model operations: service create/describe/list/update/delete, pause/resume, deployment records and operation history; auto scaling create/describe/list/delete and default selection; connections, VPC connectors, observability configurations and native tags.
- Lifecycle mutations return OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS snapshots and atomically persist RUNNING, PAUSED or DELETED before returning; the next read sees the terminal state, and every operation record is immediately SUCCEEDED. Pause and deployment require RUNNING; resume requires PAUSED. No background timer or runtime work is scheduled.
- Every input is checked against the model's required, length, range, pattern and enum constraints and fails InvalidRequestException; a source needs exactly one repository, and CPU and memory must be one of the documented values, checked independently without a runtime sizing matrix.
- Auto scaling and observability configurations have monotonically increasing revisions and Latest flags for the highest revision of each name; name-only and name/revision partial ARNs resolve the latest active matching revision. Lists default LatestOnly to true; unfiltered configuration lists omit inactive revisions, while name-filtered lists include retained tombstones.
- An account/Region-local DefaultConfiguration auto scaling revision is materialized lazily with MinSize=1, MaxSize=25 and MaxConcurrency=100. UpdateDefaultAutoScalingConfiguration changes the default; services without an ARN select the latest active revision of its name. Associated and default configurations cannot be deleted.
- Connections remain PENDING_HANDSHAKE; VPC connectors and observability configurations are ACTIVE records. Deletes retain INACTIVE configuration tombstones; deleted connections are removed.
- Tags are stored in resource records, with native tag operations, Resource Groups Tagging API support, account/Region isolation, shared token pagination and persistent SQLite restart coverage. Omitted MaxResults returns all matching records.
- Inventory reports RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false. Resource Groups recognizes the four official CloudFormation types; there is no invented connection type.
- CloudFormation AWS::AppRunner::Service, AWS::AppRunner::AutoScalingConfiguration, AWS::AppRunner::VpcConnector and AWS::AppRunner::ObservabilityConfiguration providers, with Ref and GetAtt, immutable configuration replacement, service updates and tag updates; native environment-variable and secret Name/Value arrays are translated to SDK maps.

- DeadLetterConfig on function creation and configuration updates sends discarded asynchronous events to a standard SQS queue or SNS topic as the execution role, with the original event body and RequestID, ErrorCode and ErrorMessage attributes; OnFailure destinations also receive their invocation record.
- AWS/Lambda metrics for every synchronous, asynchronous, event source mapping and function URL invocation, with dimension FunctionName and also Resource (function:alias or function:version) for qualified invocations: Invocations, Errors (0 or 1 per invocation, including runtime failures), DeadLetterErrors (Count, 1 per failed delivery to a dead-letter target), Duration (Milliseconds), Throttles (reserved concurrency exceeded), ConcurrentExecutions (executions in flight when an invocation starts) and IteratorAge (Milliseconds, age of the newest record in delivered stream batches).

DocumentDB /data/db named volumes retain documents across container recreation.
- CloudFormation DocumentDB/Neptune clusters and members wait for available before publishing endpoint attributes; the database details console shows mongosh or Gremlin HTTP connection commands.
- DocumentDB example: `mongosh 'mongodb://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/?authSource=admin&tls=false' --username masteruser --password`; Neptune example: `curl http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/gremlin -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"gremlin":"g.inject(1)"}'`.
- Create, describe, modify, stop, start, reboot and delete scoped DB instances; modeled duplicate, missing and state errors.
- PostgreSQL majors 14, 15, 16 (default), 17 map to postgres:<major>; MySQL 8.0 maps to mysql:8.0; MariaDB 11 maps to mariadb:11; DocumentDB and Neptune cluster members share their cluster engine; other engines and versions fail explicitly.
- Describe instances supports db-instance-id, engine and db-subnet-group exact-value filters; MaxRecords 20–100 and Marker pagination also work for subnet and parameter group lists.
- Subnet groups validate existing EC2 subnets in one VPC; parameter groups are records with engine-family validation and in-use deletion checks.
- Instance and group tags, diagnostic inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API integration.
- CloudFormation AWS::RDS::DBInstance and AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup with selected properties.
- Set rds.instances: docker to start real databases; default rds.instances: records returns available records immediately.
- Docker uses credentials and database names in engine image environment variables, free host ports bound to 127.0.0.1, and TCP plus pg_isready/mysqladmin ping/mariadb-admin ping readiness checks.
- Named volumes per account/Region/instance retain SQL data across container and persistent TinyStack restarts; available instances recreate or reattach containers from stored records.
- StopDBInstance stops the container, StartDBInstance starts it, and RebootDBInstance restarts it; TinyStack shutdown removes containers and retains volumes; reset and deletion remove containers and volumes.
- MasterUserPassword changes execute ALTER ROLE/ALTER USER in Docker; DBInstanceClass and AllocatedStorage are metadata; modifications apply immediately.
- Startup removes orphaned RDS containers and volumes whose ownership ARN has no instance record.
- Omitted DBName uses the instance identifier with hyphens replaced by underscores for the Docker database name; default AllocatedStorage is 20 GiB of metadata.
- CloudFormation DBInstance creation waits for availability before publishing endpoint attributes.
- AWS-style scoped console for databases, engine selection, connection commands and URLs, status polling, immediate password/class changes, tags, stop/start/reboot, confirmed deletion without snapshots, and subnet and parameter group creation and deletion.
- DocumentDB (Engine docdb) and Neptune (Engine neptune) SDKs share the RDS Query API for scoped cluster and member lifecycles; records mode retains the existing metadata-only behavior.
- Cluster identifiers, DocumentDB credentials, retention 1–35 days, ports 1150–65535, subnet/security-group references, encryption metadata, deletion protection and tags are validated; DocumentDB passwords are discarded after validation in records mode and retained privately in Docker mode.
- DocumentDB versions 3.6, 4.0 and 5.0 (default); Neptune versions 1.2.1.0 and 1.3.2.0 (default); default ports 27017 and 8182 respectively; stable resource IDs; Docker cluster, reader and member endpoints share one loopback host port.
- DescribeDBClusters shares both engines across RDS, DocumentDB and Neptune clients; engine, db-cluster-id and db-cluster-resource-id filters select exact values; MaxRecords 20–100 (default 100) uses stable Marker cursors.
- Cluster member endpoints and ports follow their parent cluster; DBClusterMembers tracks membership and writer metadata; cluster deletion requires no members and no deletion protection; DocumentDB/Neptune also require SkipFinalSnapshot=true.
- CloudFormation AWS::DocDB::DBCluster/DBInstance and AWS::Neptune::DBCluster/DBInstance share a provider: selected mutable properties and tags update, immutable properties replace, version changes fail and roll back; Ref and cluster/instance endpoint attributes are supported.
- DocumentDB/Neptune cluster/member inventory records mark RecordsOnly=true in records mode; RGTA uses rds:cluster/rds:db ARN types and Resource Groups selects AWS::DocDB and AWS::Neptune resource types; Terraform endpoint overrides include rds, docdb and neptune; console groups both under RDS.
- CreateDBSnapshot, DescribeDBSnapshots, DeleteDBSnapshot and same-account/Region CopyDBSnapshot for standalone RDS instances; lowercase identifiers and local ARNs, manual snapshot metadata, creating-to-available status and 0-to-100 progress, modeled duplicate/missing/state errors.
- DescribeDBSnapshots supports instance/snapshot identifiers, DbiResourceId, manual or automated type selection, db-instance-id (including ARNs), db-snapshot-id, dbi-resource-id, snapshot-type and engine exact filters; MaxRecords 20–100 and Marker pagination.
- RestoreDBInstanceFromDBSnapshot creates an independent instance from captured engine, version, storage, database and credential settings; selected class/storage/subnet/parameter-group overrides and tags; records mode restores metadata only.
- DeleteDBInstance accepts FinalDBSnapshotIdentifier when SkipFinalSnapshot is false (the default); final manual snapshots survive instance deletion; conflicting skip/final identifiers and snapshot name collisions fail before instance removal.
- Snapshot ARN tags support AddTagsToResource, RemoveTagsFromResource, ListTagsForResource, diagnostic inventory, Resource Groups and RGTA; CopyTags merges source snapshot tags with explicit overrides; CopyTagsToSnapshot controls instance-to-snapshot tags.
- Docker snapshots and copies use isolated, ownership-labeled data volumes; a helper using the engine image copies the volume while a running source container is paused, then resumes it even after a failed copy; restore copies the snapshot volume into a new instance volume.
- Snapshot deletion and reset remove owned snapshot volumes; snapshots retain volumes across shutdown and persistent restart, with startup orphan cleanup; failed copies remove their helper and partial destination volume.
- CloudFormation AWS::RDS::DBInstance accepts DBSnapshotIdentifier for restore and CopyTagsToSnapshot; restore creation waits for availability before endpoint publication.
- Aurora PostgreSQL (17.7 default; 16.11, 16.6, 15.10) and Aurora MySQL (8.0.mysql_aurora.3.12.0 default; 3.11.1 and 3.08.0 with the same prefix) use PostgreSQL major images and mysql:8.0 respectively; ports default to 5432 and 3306.
- Aurora clusters create one Docker container shared by all member instances; creating transitions to available after readiness, and cluster, reader and member endpoints publish the same loopback host port.
- Aurora supports DatabaseName, validated master credentials, ManageMasterUserPassword with an active Secrets Manager MasterUserSecret, HTTP endpoint flags and EnableHttpEndpoint/DisableHttpEndpoint, and stored ServerlessV2ScalingConfiguration.
- Modify Aurora credentials, retention, security groups, deletion protection, HTTP settings and scaling metadata; StopDBCluster/StartDBCluster control the shared engine and stop rolls back Data API transactions.
- CreateDBClusterSnapshot, DescribeDBClusterSnapshots, DeleteDBClusterSnapshot and final snapshots on Aurora cluster deletion; Docker snapshots copy a paused source volume, records mode captures metadata; deletion requires no members and disabled deletion protection.

### Developer Tools

#### AWS Amplify Hosting

Store Hosting apps, branches, jobs, domain associations, webhooks and backend environment metadata without builds, deployments or DNS.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 34.

- 34 of 37 pinned REST JSON operations, using the official AWS SDK v2, with account and Region isolation and SQLite restart coverage.
- App and branch CRUD stores build specs, environment variables, redirect rules, auth settings, roles and configuration; defaultDomain is the deterministic placeholder <appId>.amplifyapp.com.
- Basic auth credentials are stored but omitted from app, branch, nested auto-branch configuration and inventory responses; accessToken and oauthToken are validated then discarded, never returned.
- StartJob accepts RELEASE and RETRY: jobs remain PENDING until StopJob sets CANCELLED. RETRY allocates a new monotonic branch-local ID and copies source commit metadata; GetJob returns no steps or artifacts.
- CreateDeployment records a CREATED manual job and optional fileMap with inert amplify.invalid zip or per-file URLs; StartDeployment changes it to PENDING or records a source URL without fetching it.
- Domain association CRUD always reports PENDING_VERIFICATION, unverified subdomains and no DNS records, including custom certificates; no real DNS or certificate provisioning.
- Webhook CRUD returns inert amplify.invalid URLs; backend environment Create/Get/List/Delete stores stack and artifact names without creating resources (the model has no UpdateBackendEnvironment).
- TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource for apps and branches, Resource Groups Tagging API integration, inventory with RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false, and AWS::Amplify::App/Branch/Domain resource-group types.
- Every input is checked against the model's required, length, range, pattern and enum constraints and fails BadRequestException; tag sets follow the shared tagging limits and CUSTOM certificates need customCertificateArn.
- Token pagination with common.Page: apps default/max 100; other collections default/max 50; model maxResults=0 uses the default.
- App deletion cascades to child records; branch deletion removes its jobs and webhooks.
- CloudFormation AWS::Amplify::App, AWS::Amplify::Branch and AWS::Amplify::Domain providers with SDK lifecycle tests; Terraform app and branch apply/update/destroy cases.

### Internet of Things

#### AWS IoT Wireless

Store LoRaWAN resources and simulate local uplinks through the IoT MQTT broker and topic rules.

**Execution:** Local simulated uplinks through IoT MQTT and rules; durable downlink records and deterministic multicast/FUOTA worker; no radio transport. **Selected operations:** 68.

- 68 REST JSON operations with generated ValidationException constraints; destinations, LoRaWAN and Sidewalk device profiles, service profiles, LoRaWAN devices and gateways, multicast groups and FUOTA tasks.
- Destinations validate existing TinyStack IAM roles and IoT topic rules or publishable MQTT topics; devices validate destinations and profile references, activation mode and unique DevEui; gateways enforce unique GatewayEui.
- Things and gateway certificates associate with real TinyStack IoT resources; lookup devices and gateways by ID, EUI or associated thing name.
- TestWirelessDevice commits a simulated uplink before publishing through IoT Core: MQTT destinations deliver to subscribers and RuleName destinations invoke that rule using Basic Ingest, including SQS actions.
- Uplinks contain WirelessDeviceId, base64 PayloadData (Test), and WirelessMetadata.LoRaWAN. FPort is the first configured application port or 1; data rate 3, frequency 868300000 Hz, RSSI -64 and SNR 9.5 are deterministic. All gateways in the account and Region participate; last-uplink timestamps and gateway Connected status derive only from this traffic.
- Device and multicast downlinks queue durably without transmission; list device queues with pagination and delete a MessageId or * for all messages.
- Multicast device and FUOTA device/group associations; multicast sessions become Session_Set at their start time and return to Pending after SessionTimeout seconds or cancellation. FUOTA tasks progress FuotaSession_Waiting to In_FuotaSession to FuotaDone, with a 0.6-second session and Successful associated device status.
- A services/background.Group worker visits a durable aws/iotwireless/index every 200 milliseconds, claims transitions in transactions and resumes after SQLite restart; FUOTA firmware references must name existing TinyStack S3 objects and IAM roles.
- Stored service and per-resource log levels; GetServiceEndpoint returns this TinyStack endpoint for CUPS and its ws/wss equivalent for LNS.
- Tags on all seven resource kinds, inventory, Resource Groups and Resource Groups Tagging API; list pagination in storage key order and idempotent create tokens.
- CloudFormation Destination, DeviceProfile, ServiceProfile, MulticastGroup and FuotaTask, with immutable destination name and profile name/LoRaWAN replacement; mutable fields and tags update in place. FUOTA LoRaWAN.StartTime starts the task after associations.
- Terraform AWS provider 5.100.0 has no iotwireless resources or service endpoint key (verified complete upstream source tree); no Terraform resources, endpoint override or update-apply count changes.

[Supported operations](iotwireless.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](iotwireless.md#limitations-and-future-work)

- Creation tags and atomic TagResource/UntagResource on vaults/plans with shared tag validation and 50-tag limit; paginated ListTags and Resource Groups Tagging API integration.
- Deterministic ID/name sorting, MaxResults 1-1000, resume-after-deletion cursors bound to account, Region, operation and filter/parent; vault-type/shared and IncludeDeleted filters.
- Account/Region isolation, SQLite restart and shared reset; generic inventory, official console catalogue icon and Terraform backup endpoint.

#### AWS Resource Explorer

Search TinyStack inventory using regional indexes and views.

**Execution:** Live regional inventory search; records-only control plane. **Selected operations:** 20.

- Create and update finish synchronously as ACTIVE; delete removes the index, its views and default association synchronously and returns DELETED. One index per Region and one AGGREGATOR per account.
- Search and ListResources evaluate the query and the view filter as AWS documents: keywords are joined with OR, and that group and every filter with AND; a filter's comma-separated values are alternatives, a trailing * matches any suffix and a leading - excludes matches. Filters: accountid:, id:, region: (global resources report the Region global), resourcetype:service:type, service:, tag:key=value, tag:all, tag:none, tag.key: and tag.value:; tag filters need a view that includes tags. Keywords match the ARN or name case-insensitively as substrings. Quoted phrases, escapes, other prefixes and boolean words fail ValidationException.
- Search uses listing.Scoped and ARN order. Count.TotalResources counts all matches before common.Page pagination. Properties contain tags only when the view includes tags. LastReportedAt is the local inventory snapshot time; the inventory has no AWS discovery timestamps.
- ListSupportedResourceTypes derives its deterministic type list from the currently populated regional inventory, not a static AWS catalogue.
- GetDefaultView returns an empty response when the index has no default view, and ResourceNotFoundException when there is no regional index. Index and view tags live in their records and are visible to inventory, Resource Groups and Resource Groups Tagging API.
- CloudFormation AWS::ResourceExplorer2::Index, AWS::ResourceExplorer2::View and AWS::ResourceExplorer2::DefaultViewAssociation; Terraform aws_resourceexplorer2_index and aws_resourceexplorer2_view with resourceexplorer2 endpoint.

URLs are stored verbatim and never fetched or validated as templates; artifact responses expose the URL under Info.TemplateUrl.

Terraform portfolio, product and both portfolio association resources and endpoint configuration are covered.

- Twenty-two REST JSON operations with model constraints reported as BadRequestException.
- Create, describe, list, update and delete flows; StartFlow and StopFlow use STANDBY, STARTING, ACTIVE, STOPPING, UPDATING and DELETING states. A durable partition-wide index is claimed transactionally every 100 milliseconds, with one deterministic transition per visit and recovery after SQLite restart.
- Sources with RTP, RTP-FEC, RIST, Zixi push and SRT listener/caller records, up to two sources with failover configuration; SRT merge is rejected.
- Outputs with RTP, RTP-FEC, RIST, Zixi push/pull and SRT listener/caller records, update and removal; up to 50 outputs per flow.
- Grant, update, revoke and page entitlements; cross-account sources resolve enabled entitlements in the same Region and require the receiving account to be a subscriber.
- VPC interface records validate existing TinyStack EC2 subnets/security groups in the same VPC and Availability Zone, and existing account IAM roles; Zixi static-key and SRT password encryption validate existing Secrets Manager secrets in the same account and Region.
- Tags on flow, source, output and entitlement records (CreateFlow FlowTags or TagResource), inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API integration; list pagination follows storage key order.
- CloudFormation AWS::MediaConnect::Flow, FlowSource, FlowOutput, FlowEntitlement and FlowVpcInterface with specification-driven replacement and complete in-place template updates.
- Terraform provider 5.100 has no MediaConnect resources (verified internal/service/mediaconnect at v5.100.0); endpoint key and local Terraform CLI override are supplied; no resource/update-apply count changes.

#### API Gateway HTTP and WebSocket APIs

Manage and invoke HTTP and WebSocket APIs with routes, stages, deployments and Lambda integrations.

**Execution:** Local behavior. **Selected operations:** 39.

- AWS_IAM requires a SigV4 caller, verifies signatures in identity.mode verify, and evaluates execute-api:Invoke identity policies in authorization soft/enforce; soft denials appear in the request inspector.
- API, route, integration, deployment, stage and authorizer CRUD.
- Auto-deploy stages and Lambda proxy payload formats 1.0 and 2.0.
- HTTP forwarding, JWT and Lambda authorizers, access logs.
- AWS-style console for scoped HTTP API creation and CORS settings, routes, Lambda/HTTP integrations, JWT/Lambda authorizers, auto/manual stages, deployment snapshots, API/stage tags, and explicit deployed-stage request testing.
- With authorization on, Lambda proxy integrations need the function policy to allow apigateway.amazonaws.com with the route's execute-api ARN as aws:SourceArn; a denied invocation answers 500 Internal Server Error in enforce mode and is recorded in soft mode.
- Lambda authorizers need the function policy to allow apigateway.amazonaws.com with arn:aws:execute-api:<region>:<account>:<api-id>/authorizers/<authorizer-id> as aws:SourceArn; a denied invocation answers 500.
- AWS/ApiGateway metrics for requests to a deployed stage, with dimensions ApiId and ApiId with Stage: Count, 4xx, 5xx, Latency and IntegrationLatency (Milliseconds; only for requests that reached the integration).
- WebSocket APIs select custom routes using $request.body.<field> dotted paths, with $default fallback for missing, invalid or unmatched message selections; $connect and $disconnect invoke lifecycle integrations.
- WebSocket Lambda AWS_PROXY integrations receive CONNECT, MESSAGE and DISCONNECT request contexts, connection IDs, timestamps, source IP, API/stage/domain information and connect headers/query parameters; non-2xx connect responses reject the handshake.
- WebSocket MOCK integrations return status 200 with an empty body; $default route response CRUD enables two-way message responses from Lambda or MOCK integrations; other routes are one-way.
- WebSocket execute-api endpoints support host-style and /_aws/execute-api/<api-id>/<stage> addressing, auto/manual deployment snapshots, 10-minute idle and 2-hour lifetime limits; connections are memory-only and close on shutdown/reset.
- API key selection expressions accept $request.header.x-api-key (the default) or $context.authorizer.usageIdentifierKey and are stored for both protocols.
- HTTP-only CORS, quick-create and IP address settings are rejected on WebSocket APIs; WebSocket-only route responses and ApiKeyRequired=true are rejected on HTTP APIs.

#### AWS Global Accelerator

Store standard accelerators, listeners and regional endpoint groups with local endpoint validation, CloudFormation and Terraform support; no traffic forwarding.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 22.

- Twenty-two pinned AWS JSON 1.1 operations for standard accelerator lifecycle, attributes, listeners, endpoint groups, endpoint membership and accelerator tags; generated InvalidArgumentException model validation.
- Account-global records use request.GlobalScope with an empty Region. Like IAM and Route 53, requests signed in any Region share the same records. AWS serves its global API only in us-west-2; use us-west-2 for SDK/provider compatibility (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/api/API_UpdateAccelerator.html).
- CreateAccelerator and UpdateAccelerator return IN_PROGRESS snapshots and atomically persist DEPLOYED; all later Describe/List calls and restarts see DEPLOYED without timers or health probes.
- Deterministic allocation uses the lowest free slot 1..254 per account: 192.0.2.<slot> and 198.51.100.<slot>, plus 2001:db8::<2*slot+1 in hex> and 2001:db8::<2*slot+2 in hex> for DUAL_STACK. Addresses are unique among live accelerators in an account, remain stable through disable/type updates/restart and may be reused after deletion. Exhausting the 254-slot local documentation address pool returns LimitExceededException; this is a TinyStack fixture capacity, not an AWS quota.
- DNS labels are a followed by 16 hex digits derived from SHA-256 of the ARN, ending .awsglobalaccelerator.com; dual-stack adds .dualstack.awsglobalaccelerator.com. The a prefix follows AWS documentation (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/api/API_Accelerator.html).
- Accelerators must be disabled and have no listeners before deletion. Listeners must have no endpoint groups before deletion. Port ranges must not overlap within a listener or across listeners of the same accelerator and protocol.
- One endpoint group per Region per listener; endpoint IDs are checked via exported EC2/ELBv2 methods in the endpoint group Region and account. Supports existing application/network load balancer ARNs, running EC2 instance IDs and Elastic IP allocation IDs; missing references fail explicitly.
- Endpoint descriptions remain INITIAL (unprobed); HealthReason is absent/null. AWS health states are INITIAL, HEALTHY and UNHEALTHY (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/api/API_EndpointDescription.html). Weight, client IP preservation, port overrides, health configuration and traffic dial are stored; interval must be 10 or 30 seconds.
- Flow log attributes require an existing local S3 bucket in the same account (any Region); enabling requires bucket and prefix. No log objects are written and S3 delivery policies are not evaluated.
- Create idempotency tokens persist with their resource and reject reuse with different parameters. List operations page in storage key order. Tags live in accelerator records and integrate with inventory, Resource Groups and Resource Groups Tagging.
- CloudFormation AWS::GlobalAccelerator::Accelerator, AWS::GlobalAccelerator::Listener and AWS::GlobalAccelerator::EndpointGroup; supported mutable properties update in place, Listener.AcceleratorArn and EndpointGroup.ListenerArn/EndpointGroupRegion replace resources.
- Terraform globalaccelerator endpoint key and aws_globalaccelerator_accelerator, aws_globalaccelerator_listener and aws_globalaccelerator_endpoint_group lifecycle case using a dedicated local Elastic IP; SDK v2 and SQLite restart coverage.

#### AWS Private CA

Store private certificate authorities, their revocation settings and tags as records without any cryptography.

**Execution:** Configuration records only. **Selected operations:** 9.

- Nine pinned AWS JSON 1.1 operations: Create, Describe, List, Update, Delete and Restore for certificate authorities, plus TagCertificateAuthority, UntagCertificateAuthority and ListTags, with AWS SDK v2 integration.
- ROOT and SUBORDINATE authorities validate the documented key and signing algorithm pairs (RSA with SHA*WITHRSA, EC with SHA*WITHECDSA, ML-DSA with its own name, SM2 with SM3WITHSM2 in China Regions), the X.500 subject fields with their model limits, usage mode and key storage security standard.
- CreateCertificateAuthority honours IdempotencyToken for five minutes and returns the same ARN for a repeated token.
- CRL and OCSP settings are validated metadata: a disabled block carries only Enabled=false, an enabled CRL names an S3 bucket that must exist in the account and Region, CNAMEs take no protocol prefix; no CRL is written and no responder runs.
- New authorities start PENDING_CERTIFICATE. UpdateCertificateAuthority changes the status of ACTIVE and DISABLED authorities only and replaces the supplied CRL or OCSP block; a rejected update leaves the record unchanged.
- DeleteCertificateAuthority keeps the authority as DELETED for PermanentDeletionTimeInDays (7 to 30, default 30) with RestorableUntil; an ACTIVE authority must be disabled first, RestoreCertificateAuthority returns the status it had, and an authority past its window disappears (removed lazily on read).
- Tags on create and with TagCertificateAuthority, UntagCertificateAuthority (a tag with a value is removed only when it matches) and ListTags, plus Resource Groups Tagging API support.
- AWS::ACMPCA::CertificateAuthority CloudFormation resource with Ref and Fn::GetAtt Arn; revocation configuration and tags update in place and other properties replace the authority.
- RecordsOnly=true / ExecutionReady=false inventory, official AWS Private CA icon and Terraform acmpca endpoint key.

AWS ARNs from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/securityhub/describe-standards.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark.html; CIS 1.2.0 uses arn:aws:securityhub:::ruleset/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/1.2.0, others use arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/<standard>/v/<version>, including nist-800-53/v/5.0.0.
- Catalogue ARNs (replace <region>): arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/aws-foundational-security-best-practices/v/1.0.0; arn:aws:securityhub:::ruleset/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/1.2.0; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/1.4.0; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/3.0.0; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/pci-dss/v/3.2.1; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/nist-800-53/v/5.0.0.
- EnableDefaultStandards defaults to true and enables AWS Foundational Security Best Practices v1.0.0 and CIS v1.2.0, matching https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-settingup.html. Subscriptions become READY immediately and disappear synchronously on disable (response status DELETING).
- Every input is checked against the model's required, length, range, pattern and enum constraints and fails InvalidInputException; BatchImportFindings checks each finding separately.
- BatchImportFindings accepts 1–100 ASFF records, validates required fields and supported model constraints, reports per-entry failures and replaces records keyed by ProductArn plus Id. Missing Workflow and RecordState default to NEW and ACTIVE.
- GetFindings string filters: EQUALS/PREFIX/NOT_EQUALS on Id, ProductArn, GeneratorId, AwsAccountId, SeverityLabel, WorkflowStatus, RecordState, ResourceType, ResourceId and ComplianceStatus; inclusive RFC3339 Start/End dates on CreatedAt/UpdatedAt. Fields use AND, positive terms within a field use OR, negative terms exclude all their values. Positive and negative terms cannot mix. Unsupported fields/comparisons fail explicitly.
- GetFindings supports multiple asc/desc sort criteria on supported scalar filter fields plus Title, CreatedAt and UpdatedAt; dates compare instants, ties preserve storage order. Pagination uses snapshot positions, default/maximum 100; concurrent mutations can change page boundaries. Other record lists use storage key order.
- BatchUpdateFindings stores Workflow, Severity, Note, Confidence, Criticality, VerificationState, Types, UserDefinedFields and RelatedFindings and updates UpdatedAt. Unknown identifiers are unprocessed.
- Insights validate the same filters and group by supported string filter fields; computed results count distinct values once per finding and rank counts descending with lexical ties.
- Custom action targets store names/descriptions without invoking actions. Hub tags integrate with Resource Groups Tagging API and RecordsOnly inventory. Records survive SQLite restart.
- CloudFormation AWS::SecurityHub::Hub, AWS::SecurityHub::Standard and AWS::SecurityHub::Insight; Terraform aws_securityhub_account, aws_securityhub_standards_subscription, aws_securityhub_action_target and aws_securityhub_insight.

- Scoped/filter-bound deterministic pagination with default 100 and positive requested sizes capped at 1000; stable ID/key order and resume after cursor deletion.

- CloudFormation FileSystem/MountTarget/AccessPoint Ref/GetAtt, mutable throughput/security-group/tag updates and immutable replacement. - Multipart upload lifecycle and atomic completion, concatenating part files without buffering the complete object.
- Disk-backed objects and parts in both storage modes, streaming HTTP downloads including byte ranges, startup migration and orphan collection with transactional counts for shared file references.
- Streaming HTTP uploads for PutObject and UploadPart directly into disk-backed blob files with bounded memory, supporting ordinary, chunked and aws-chunked formats with trailing checksum validation.
- Stored object checksums (CRC32, CRC32C, CRC64NVME by default, SHA-1, SHA-256) returned with ChecksumMode, composite and full-object multipart checksums, kept through copies and versions.
- Versioning, null versions and delete markers.
- Presigned requests, bucket CORS and notifications to SQS, SNS, Lambda and EventBridge.
- Bucket lifecycle and encryption configuration are stored.
- AWS-style console for scoped bucket creation, empty/delete, folder and object browsing, uploads/downloads/copies, version deletion, object tags and bucket configuration.
- Bucket policies participate in gateway soft/enforce authorization, including cross-account bucket/object access and owning-root policy recovery.
- With authorization on, notification destinations (SQS, SNS, Lambda) need their resource policy to allow s3.amazonaws.com for the bucket (aws:SourceArn, aws:SourceAccount); enforce mode fails PutBucketNotificationConfiguration with InvalidArgument, unless SkipDestinationValidation is set, and denies later deliveries, while soft mode records the denied check.
- Object Lock at bucket creation or on a versioned bucket: GOVERNANCE and COMPLIANCE retention, legal hold and default bucket retention; deleting a locked version fails AccessDenied, COMPLIANCE retention cannot be shortened, and GOVERNANCE is bypassed with x-amz-bypass-governance-retention (s3:BypassGovernanceRetention when authorization is on).
- Browser POST uploads (multipart/form-data to the bucket): ${filename} keys, policy expiration and eq/starts-with/content-length-range conditions, every field covered by the policy, SigV4 policy signatures in verify mode, success_action_status 200/201/204 and success_action_redirect; the upload is authorized and stored as PutObject.

[Supported operations](s3.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](s3.md#limitations-and-future-work)

## Keep the catalogue current

Feature descriptions live in `docs/catalog.json`; operation counts come from registered profiles.
Update the catalogue with each delivered service or feature, then run `task docs:generate` and
`task docs:check`. CI rejects stale generated pages and undocumented registered services.

See the [documentation workflow](../development/documentation.md) for maintenance.
Proposed additions remain in the [future catalogue](../roadmap/catalogue.md).
